faq: How do you know who is a good lead?
You tell us who you want to serve, and which past customers were the best. We compare the leads with that, and we ask you to confirm our ratings on a handful so we judge as you would.
Do I have to share customer details?
We need the enquiry text and source, not payment details. Remove names or emails if you prefer, because the review works on what people asked for and how they found you.
Will you filter out leads automatically?
On Premium we write polite auto-reply wording for poor-fit enquiries, such as pointing them to a better option. We do not delete leads or block anyone unfairly.
Will fewer leads be a bad thing?
Not always. If the changes reduce unsuitable enquiries, you may see fewer but better ones. We explain what to expect, so you are not alarmed by a lower count.

desc:
A lead quality review checks whether the people contacting you match the customers you want to serve. Ecom Swift LLC reads a sample of your recent leads, traces why poor-fit enquiries arrive and gives you a plain report with changes to your forms and targeting.

## What is a lead quality review?

A lead quality review is a close look at the enquiries you receive, compared against your ideal customer. We read each lead, note what they asked for and mark how well they fit your service, location and budget. Then we look for patterns in where the poor-fit ones came from and what attracted them.

The result is an explanation, not just a score. You learn why the wrong people are reaching you and what could change that.

## Why the wrong leads cost more than you think

A crowded inbox looks like success, but every unsuitable enquiry costs time. Someone has to read it, reply, take a call and eventually say no. That effort comes straight out of the hours you could spend on people who are ready to buy.

Poor-fit leads also distort your picture of what works. If a campaign brings many enquiries that never convert, it may seem to be doing well on a simple count. Without a quality check, you might spend more on the very source that wastes your time.

## How a review improves your results

Better-fit leads are usually the result of clearer messages, not more advertising. When your offer says who it is for and what it costs to work with you, people who do not match tend to stay away. A form with a few qualifying questions helps both sides, because the lead understands what you need and you understand what they want.

Fewer, better enquiries can mean shorter sales conversations and less time lost. A review cannot control who contacts you, and results depend on your market, but it shows which small changes reduce the mismatch.

## What a great review includes

- A fair sample of recent leads, drawn from different sources.
- A written description of your ideal customer to compare against.
- A fit rating for each lead with a short reason.
- A comparison of fit by source and campaign.
- Notes on how your page wording may attract the wrong people.
- A look at the form, including missing or confusing questions.
- Suggested changes to ad audiences or keywords where they apply.
- Qualifying questions written in your voice.
- Polite auto-reply wording for people who are not a fit.
- A priority list of fixes and a plan to re-check.

## What we do

We ask you to describe who you serve best and who you do not. You share the leads in a sheet, your CRM or your inbox, with any outcome notes you have. We read them, rate them and group the poor-fit ones by cause, such as an unclear offer, a wide ad audience or a form that asks too little.

The report explains each cause and lists changes in order of value. Larger packages review more leads, compare sources, improve form questions, suggest offer wording and write qualifying questions for specific services. The largest package adds suggestions for ad audiences and keywords, auto-reply wording and a review call with a plan to check again after changes. We do not change your live ads or forms unless you ask for that as separate work.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Define your ideal customer in plain terms before the review.
- Include leads that did not buy as well as those who did.
- Be honest about which enquiries wasted your time.
- Change one thing at a time so you can see its effect.
- Check again after a few weeks.

**Avoid:**
- Judging a lead only by the size of the job.
- Making your form so strict that good people give up.
- Ignoring the source of each lead.
- Blaming the traffic when the page wording is unclear.
- Deleting old leads before they have been reviewed.

## Who this service is for

This service suits an owner whose inbox is full but whose calendar is not. It also helps a business running paid campaigns that suspects the audience is too wide. A service provider with a high price point, who needs serious buyers rather than browsers, will see the clearest value.

## What we need from you

Share a recent list of leads with names removed or reduced to the details needed, such as source, request and outcome. Tell us who your best customers are. We never need passwords. If we need to see forms or ad settings, access is given as a collaborator, staff or team user, and you can hide customer contact details when you prefer.
